result.title: SurgEye: Instruction Tuning-Free Perception-Reasoning Framework for Surgical Scene Understanding
result.summary: Surgical scene understanding is pivotal for computer-assisted intervention, yet demands compositional reasoning across instruments, anatomy, and workflow. Existing surgical vision-language models rely on instruction tuning with large-scale question-answer pairs, entailing laborious data curation and costly retraining. To bridge this gap, we propose SurgEye, a perception-reasoning framework that grounds reasoning in a vision foundation model without instruction tuning. Specifically, we devise Routed Multi-Task Perception (RMP) that routes the vision foundation model through task-specific pathways learned from public perception labels, producing spatial and temporal evidence. We further introduce Agentic Compositional Reasoning (ACR) that employs a frozen large language model to coordinate RMP specialists and temporal memory as callable tools, composing evidence across tasks and time into grounded answers. Moreover, we construct SurgEye-Bench spanning eight surgical procedures, pairing each question with perception labels for verifiable evaluation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SurgEye outperforms state-of-the-arts in surgical reasoning. The source code will be available.

AI.brief_summary: 提出无需指令微调的手术场景理解框架：将视觉基础模型按任务路由为多个感知专家以产出空间与时序证据，再由冻结 LLM 以可调用工具方式组合这些证据作答，并构建带感知标签、可验证评测的 SurgEye-Bench。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「感知专家作可调用工具 + 跨任务跨时间证据组合」的外化分工，可能为 LVR 中按需获取与筛选视觉证据、以及 THINK/LOOK 组合与停止条件提供对照线索，但论文以工具调用替代内部 latent 状态，需核查其证据选择与计算成本。
